newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS WINS NINTH GAME IN JAYS' ROUT OF RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS WINS NINTH GAME IN JAYS' ROUT OF RANGERS.

text.p: Everything was beautiful for Roger Clemens Monday as he become the first nine-game winner in the majors thanks to the Toronto Blue Jays' 8-1 rout of the Texas Rangers.

"The defence was beautiful, our defence has been outstanding," Clemens said. "The hitters were beautiful. Tonight the hitters deserved the credit, they set the tempo. Hopefully, it'll be a roller coaster and keep feeding on itself."
Clemens (9-0) allowed one run over seven innings and won his sixth straight start, giving up four hits with four walks and seven strikeouts. Paul Quantrill finished up with two scorelesss innings.

Clemens lowered his league-best ERA to 1.81 and defeated the Rangers for the second time this season, allowing just two runs and six hits over 14 innings. His only mistake was a solo home run by Juan Gonzalez in the fourth inning.
"I see him pitching better than ever, in, out, up and down, hitting his spots," Texas manager Johnny Oates said.
Ruben Sierra went 3-for-3 with two RBI to lead the Jays' 13-hit attack. Orlando Merced and Ed Sprague homered.
"It was something we were waiting for for a while," said Sprague. "We gave Roger some hitting room against a great club."
Sierra, playing for his fifth team in three seasons, is 4-for-10 with two RBI since joining Toronto. He was released by the Cincinnati Reds earlier this month.
"I know I can still play, I have a lot of years to go," Sierra said. "I'm going to stay focused and come back."
Texas starter Julio Santana (2-2) took the loss.

At Minnesota, Edgar Martinez drilled a pair of three-run homers, Jay Buhner also homered twice and Joey Cora ran his hitting streak to 21 games with a leadoff blast as the Seattle Mariners cruised to a 13-8 victory over the Twins.
Seattle got hits from all of its starters except Ken Griffey Jr, who leads the majors with 22 homers. Martinez's six RBI were a career high.
Cora led off the game with his fifth homer -- on an 0-2 pitch -- to tie the all-time club hitting streak.
Russ Davis also homered for Seattle.

In Chicago, Marquis Grissom's three hits and Jim Thome's three RBI spearheaded an offensive attack that saw all nine starters reach base and eight different players score as the Cleveland Indians routed the White Sox 10-4.

Manny Ramirez added three hits and two RBI as the Indians banged out 13 hits. The only starter who didn't score was Dave Justice, who with a single and two walks reached base for the 43rd time in 44 games.

The game marked the first time Albert Belle played against his former club. He got a single in his final at-bat to extend his hitting streak to 21 games, matching his career high and keeping him even with Cora for longest in the majors.
Chicago got back-to-back homers by Mike Cameron and Frank Thomas in the first.
Chicago's Tony Pena caught his 1,927th game, tying Jim Sundberg for fourth place on the all-time list.

In New York, B.J. Surhoff drove in three runs, including a two-run single that capped a six-run seventh inning, as the Baltimore Orioles handed Andy Pettitte consecutive losses for the first time in 53 starts in an 8-6 win over the Yankees.

Brady Anderson also drove in three runs as the first-place Orioles won for the seventh time in their last nine games and increased their cushion over the Yankees in the American League East to seven games.
It was the first meeting between the teams since last year's league championship series, won by the Yankees 4-1.
Pettitte (6-3) had not lost two straight starts since August 1995. Shawn Boskie (2-2) pitched a scoreless sixth inning to get the win.
In Detroit, Omar Olivares tossed a four-hit shutout and Travis Fryman drove in three runs as the Tigers beat the Anaheim Angels 6-0.
Olivares (3-3) walked two and struck out four and didn't allow a hit over the final 4 1/3 innings for Detroit, which has won six of its last nine games.
Angels starter Chuck Finley (2-4) was the loser.
Anaheim lost for just the third time in its last 14 games.
In Kansas City, Scott Spiezio singled in Jose Canseco in the top of the 11th as the Oakland Atheletics edged the Royals 2-1 for just their fifth win in 19 games.
Royals' starter Kevin Appier recorded a season-high 10 strikeouts, extending his own club record by fanning at least 10 for the 19th time.
In Boston, Tim Naehring's ninth-inning double off the left-field wall scored Wil Cordero and pinch-runner Jeff Frye to give the Red Sox a 3-2 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers.
Mike Matheny had a two-run homer for Milwaukee.
